one_pager.big_idea: Scientists do not just publish what they think: other scientists check their work first (peer review), and good scientists welcome criticism and change their work because of it.
goals: I can write a fact-check report that gives a verdict on the three-point scale with a confidence level, using our data as evidence.
I can review another group's report like a journal reviewer, with specific and helpful comments, and revise our own report in response to a review.

flow.what: Hand back each group's plan and data sheet (or a printed photo) with a report template; show the section-owner chart. Lead Scientist gives out sections; everyone finds the data they need. Slides 1 to 2.

How a journal decides: authors, editor, reviewers, revise, publish. 'Even Nobel Prize winners get reviewer comments.' Question: 'Why would scientists ask someone else to find problems in their work?' Slide 3.

Sample report extract (the lid report); model one reviewer comment (major issue) with the frame; major versus minor and the Low, Medium, High confidence scale. Pairs find two more problems (worksheet Core 1). Slides 4 to 5.

Groups write the report in parallel, one section each. Teacher pushes for numbers in evidence, units, the right graph type and honest limitations. At minute 18 (last 3 minutes of the draft) groups agree the verdict and confidence together. Slides 6 to 7.
Swap reports: Group 1 and 4, 2 and 5, 3 and 6. Reviewers use the checklist, check one mean with a calculator, write 3 to 5 comment slips (at least one strength) and choose a recommendation. Slide 8.

Reports returned with reviews: reply, fix major issues, fill in the revision log (5 min). Self-assessment slip (4 min). Week 10 talk frame, talk parts and exit ticket (2 min). Collect every report, revision log and reviewer checklist. Slides 9 to 11.

one_pager.practical: No practical. Each group drafts a four-page fact-check report from its Week 8 data (one section per role), reviews its partner group's report with the reviewer checklist and comment slips, then replies to the comments and revises its own report.
one_pager.assessment: A revised fact-check report per group with the reviewer checklist, comment slips and revision log attached, all collected: evidence for rubric strands 1 to 5 (judged per student before Week 10, with the plan, data sheet, logbook and Week 8 run sheet notes). Checklists and comment slips support strand 5, including for the reviewers. Self-assessment slips (do not change levels). Exit ticket: one change made, verdict with confidence, Week 10 talk part.
hazards: No practical hazards beyond normal classroom rules.
Feedback can feel personal: comment on the science, never on the people or their English.
one_pager.language_note: Frames for authors: 'We tested ___ by ___.' 'The mean ___ was ___ compared with ___.' 'Our verdict is ___ with ___ confidence because ___.' 'To be more confident, we would need ___.' Frames for reviewers: 'In section ___, ___. This matters because ___. We suggest ___.' 'The strongest part of this report is ___ because ___.' Chinese talk is welcome while drafting and reviewing; reports are written in English with key words in English; comments may be written in Chinese if needed, with key science words in English. Traps: 'review' is checking someone's work, not revising for a test; 'revise' means improve the work, not study; 'confidence' is about the evidence, not feeling brave; 'major' and 'minor' are about the effect on the verdict, not the length of the comment.
watch_out: The lesson is tight: keep strictly to the slide clock. Groups not finished drafting at minute 21 still swap, and reviewers comment on what is there ('Section 5 is missing' is a fair major comment).
Misconceptions: 'a good review only says nice things'; 'if reviewers find problems, our project failed'; 'Not enough evidence yet is a weak verdict'; 'high confidence means we did a lot of work'.
If time is short the draft and review are fixed: minimum 2 comment slips, revise major issues only, and the self-assessment slip can be skipped (it does not change levels).
one_pager.next_week_link: Collect every report: they are needed to judge strands 1 to 5 and prepare certificates before the Claim Busters Conference, and groups get them back at the start of Week 10 for their 2-minute talks. Every student has chosen a talk part from the talk frame. Week 10 also has the final skills check and interest survey: check the Week 1 skills check papers are filed and that there are enough fresh copies of the same paper.
